Posted February 21, 2003
(MarijuanaNews note: Documenting bad journalism is one of the key purposes of MarijuanaNews. Sometimes it is just toooo easy. One should not expect great journalism from tabloids, but can't they at least show a decent respect for the opinions of mankind. "? Apparently, not.

The Canoe chain of Sun tabloids is consistently prohibitionist in its editorial policies, although they do favor medical cannabis. (The Vancouver Sun, a quality broadsheetis the only Sun that is not a part of the chain.) Consequently, they must have been greatly disappointed to find that 70% of Canadians support decriminalization.

Rather than try to understand the reasons for this widespread support among all age groups, they have quoted only prohibitionist politicians and the head of the Canadian Police Assoc., who has consistently lied to the Canadian people about cannabis.

Stories very similar to the one below ran in all of the Canoe papers. The other Canadian papers may report the results tomorrow.

These poll results are important because the Canadian Justice Minister, Martin Cauchon has indicated that he is going to push for some sort of decriminalization in the next few months. We shall see.)

From The Calgary Sun
http://www.canoe.ca/CalgaryNews/cs.cs-02-21-0011.html

By Bill Rodgers, Ottawa Bureau Chief
February 21, 2003
See
Article From The Calgary Sun Is So Dumb That Reading It Could Cause Brain Damage.
Prohibitionist Drivel At Its Worst.

Majority wants mellower laws.7 out of 10 Canadians say decriminalize
OTTAWA -- The country is going to pot.
(MarijuanaNews note: Two word plays already. A tedious journalistic cliché.)

According to an SES/Sun Media poll, 69% of Canadians favour the decriminalization of possession of small amounts of marijuana.

The survey found Canadians who were teenagers during the " flower power " '60s were the group most likely to support easing our pot laws.

Among age groups, it showed that 76% of Canadians between the ages of 50 and 59, support decriminalization, while 72% of the 40 to 49 age group agree the laws against smoking dope should be relaxed.

The poll surveyed 1,000 people between Feb. 2 and Feb. 11. The poll is accurate plus or minus 3.1%, 19 times out of 20.

There was strong support for decriminalization in every region. Only 25% of those who responded to the survey opposed our marijuana possession laws going up in smoke.
(MarijuanaNews note: Oh so clever! Of course, possession would still remain illegal, but we mustn't let the facts get in the way of another brilliantly original bit of wordplay. Shakespeare must be green with envy.)

" The opinions of Canadians may have been influenced by numerous media stories related to the therapeutic use of marijuana for cancer patients, " said SES President Nik Nanos.
(MarijuanaNews note: Oh? Then why isn't there 70% support for the decriminalization of morphine? Could it be that Canadians don't want their children to get criminal records? Could it be that Canadians know that a dozen DEAland states have decriminalized?)

Liberal, Tory and Alliance MPs say pot shouldn't be considered a harmless recreational drug,
See
Marijuana Isn't Harmless. Okay, But Why Isn't Sold Over the Counter? Or Would You Ban Something That Causes 300,000 ER Visits Every Year, And Kills A Child Every Month? (Trick Question)

even though a Senate committee last fall recommended legalizing the smoking of pot for anybody older than 16.
(MarijuanaNews note: No, they called for the full legalization of cannabis, including growing and sales.)
See The Canadian Senate report

Doing so would make Canada one of the most cannabis-friendly nations in the world. The committee called the present criminal laws on possession of weed outdated.

At the time, the Canadian Police Association lashed out at the recommendation, calling it " a back-to-school gift for drug pushers. "
See
Canadian Police Association Demonstrates The Role of Ideology in the Maintenance of Marijuana Prohibition. Sweden Ideal While the Dutch Are the Worst. Analysis by Richard Cowan.
and
As Canada Moves Toward Some Form Of Decriminalization, Canadian Narks and Walters Escalate Lying. The New Math. Canada Replaces Mexico As Leading Supplier of Cannabis. And If You Believe That

Justice Minister Martin Cauchon doesn't plan to make the drug legal, but favours a fine instead of a prison sentence for the possession of 30 grams of weed for personal use.
See
Canadian Prime Minister Says He Has Been In Favor Of Decrim Since 1980. How Time Flies When You Are In Power. Possession Law Hostage to Medical Cannabis. Another Deadline On Taking Care of Patients.

Toronto-area Grit MP (Pickering-Ajax-Uxbridge) Dan McTeague says there needs to be a national debate on the issue.
See
Canadian Supreme Court Punts On Cannabis Cases Until Spring. The Games Governments Play Prove The Need for International Debate on Cannabis Prohibition. Special to MarijuanaNews

" As if we have not had the lesson of the destruction alcohol has reeked(sic) on families, " he said. " Do we need another form of mind-bending products that are going to ruin people's lives? "
(MarijuanaNews note: Reeked? His logic reeks. This journalism reeks, and prohibition has wreaked havoc on Canadians health.)
See
The Reality Of the Marijuana Situation In Canada: Unequal Injustice.
Alcohol Costs Canadian Health Almost 100 Times As Much As Marijuana.
Tobacco: Almost 200 As Much Article and Editorial

" It's wrong to go down that road, " said Tory MP Elsie Wayne. " That is the worst step that Canada can make right now for ... young people. "
(MarijuanaNews note: Joe Clark, the leader of the Tories, supports decrim.)

Alliance Justice critic Chuck Cadman called decriminalization a confusing message for young people because the government is also telling them to avoid drugs.
(MarijuanaNews note: Which is why Canada must ban alcohol and other adult activities?)

" Then on the other hand we send them a message from the Parliament of Canada: 'Well, we'll decriminalize it anyway.' It's just that young people take that kind of a message the wrong way, " said Cadman.
